content.text:
Current flow always invokes all four Buildx builds in sequence: server, frontend app, migrate, CLI. Caching may shorten builds but cannot prevent backend build invocation. Push runs publish digests and a complete `images.json`; manual release dispatch only warms caches. ARM dispatch publishes separate test images and must continue building all four by default.

Safe reuse invariants:

- Select the nearest successful **published release whose source is an ancestor of the current commit**. Fetch full history. Do not use the latest tag: tags are allocated before builds, so failed releases leave tags.
- Compare that release’s source with current HEAD, not `github.event.before`. This catches backend changes in skipped, failed, cancelled, or combined pushes.
- Build all three backend variants together when backend inputs change: `exposed/**`, Cargo files, `.sqlx/**`, migrations, backend Dockerfile, `.dockerignore`, or build/release machinery. Conservatively include `sqlx.toml`; backend build currently does not copy it.
- Without backend changes, copy exact `server`, `migrate`, and `cli` immutable repository digest references from validated release metadata. Require all three, correct repository/digest syntax, and accessible registry manifests. Missing baseline or unusable metadata must rebuild or fail safely.
- Always build app for the new release version; continue publishing all four versioned tags and all four manifest entries. `image.txt` and moving `server` alias should reference the selected backend digest.
- Preserve original attested image-index digests. Reused OCI revision labels and provenance correctly identify the older backend source; release-wide `source` identifies the assembled release, so expose per-image source/reuse origin if needed to avoid implying every image was rebuilt.
- Keep manual cache-warming and `cold` semantics explicit: dispatch currently publishes no release; a cold manual run should still build backend. New build-selection inputs should default to all builds for ARM compatibility.
- Serialize publishing or otherwise prevent an older concurrent run from overwriting `server`/GitHub latest after a newer run. Current workflow has no concurrency protection; nearest-ancestor discovery alone does not solve publication ordering.

Docker separation already supports this: the backend Dockerfile never copies frontend files, while `Dockerfile.frontend` builds only Node. No `docker/README.md` exists in this checkout.
